rationale: Hold, but first explicit 'soon appropriate to raise' pivot.
First hike (25bp); well-telegraphed by January's pivot.
Step-up to 50bp; 'highly attentive to inflation risks' added.
Historic 75bp hike, biggest step yet; 'strongly committed' added.
Second consecutive 75bp hike; continuation of established pace.
Third consecutive 75bp hike; fully expected continuation.
Fourth 75bp hike, but new 'cumulative tightening/lags' language hints at future deceleration.
Step down to 50bp from 75bp; meaningful deceleration.
Further deceleration to 25bp; 'inflation has eased somewhat' is first softening.
25bp hike but guidance softened to 'may be appropriate'; banking-stress caveat added.
25bp hike but 'may be appropriate' now fully conditional; read as signaling a pause.
First hold after 10 consecutive hikes; genuine regime pivot.
Hike resumes after the pause ('hawkish skip'); reversal is itself surprising.
Second hold; 'job gains have slowed' but inflation-risk language unchanged.
Third hold; well-established pause, minimal new signal.
First explicit 'inflation has eased over the past year' framing; dovish tilt (this was the 'dot plot pivot' meeting).
First explicit mention that cuts are being considered, even while saying not yet appropriate.
Near-identical language to January; repeat, low surprise.
'Lack of further progress' on inflation reverses the recent softening trend.
'Modest further progress' - improvement from May's 'lack of progress'.
New 'risks to both sides' framing drops the inflation-only focus; sets up the September cut.
First cut of the cycle, and a 50bp cut (vs. the more typical 25bp) - high surprise on size.
25bp cut; deceleration in pace from September's 50bp.
25bp cut but 'extent and timing' language reads cautious; markets took this as hawkish-leaning guidance alongside the cut.
First hold after three consecutive cuts; genuine pause signal.
Second hold; 'uncertainty has increased' is the only new note.
New explicit dual-risk framing: 'risks of higher unemployment AND higher inflation have risen'.
'Uncertainty has diminished but remains elevated' - slight de-escalation.
'Growth moderated in the first half' - a growth-outlook downgrade.
First cut after six holds; 'downside risks to employment have risen' justification.
Second consecutive cut, plus announced end of balance-sheet runoff (QT) - an added dovish/liquidity signal.
Third consecutive cut, plus a new reserve-management Treasury-purchase program - further dovish/liquidity easing.
First hold after three cuts; pause signal.
New Middle East geopolitical-risk mention added; otherwise unchanged.
Inflation concern escalates, explicitly tied to global energy prices from the geopolitical shock.
Notably terser statement format/style shift; 'will deliver price stability' reads as a harder commitment despite holding.
Same terse format repeated; less surprising now that it's established.
Hike resumes after a cutting-then-holding regime; a major, surprising reversal.
